Q18094: Capital of Hawaii, on the southeast coast of the island of Oʻahu.
Capital of the independent Kingdom of Hawaii from 1845; ʻIolani Palace is the only royal palace on US soil.
Waikīkī Beach and Diamond Head are famous sights.
Pearl Harbor, attacked by Japan on 7 December 1941, is just west of the city.
Q207429: Capital of Chiapas in southeastern Mexico.
Gateway to the Sumidero Canyon, with walls up to 1,000 m high.
Known for marimba music and its zoo of native Chiapas animals.
Q5815: City in western Siberia on the Tura River, just east of the Urals.
Founded in 1586, the first Russian town in Siberia.
Capital of Russia's main oil and gas region; Lenin's body was kept here during WWII.
Known for its hot springs and the 'Bridge of Lovers'.
Q572140: Home of the Jinxiu Yao Autonomous County, centre of the Yao people.
Known for sugar cane and the Laibin power station.
Q628: City in Lombardy at the foot of the Alps, north-east of Milan.
Its hilltop old town (Città Alta) is surrounded by Venetian walls that are a World Heritage Site.
Was one of the first and hardest-hit places in Europe in the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic.
Birthplace of the composer Gaetano Donizetti.
Q572089: City in northwestern Guangxi bordering Guizhou.
Bama county is famous as a 'longevity village' with many centenarians.
A karst region with Zhuang, Yao and Maonan minorities; known for tin mining.
Q3825: Capital of Gabon, on the Gabon Estuary near the equator.
Founded in 1849 by freed slaves from a captured slave ship; the name means 'free town' in French.
Grew rich with oil, manganese and timber exports.
Home to about a third of Gabon's people.
Q7563836: Large township 30 km north of Pretoria.
Its name is an acronym of Sotho, Shangaan, Nguni and Venda, the groups placed there under apartheid.
Part of the City of Tshwane.
Q16558: Texas's fourth-largest city, part of the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex.
Founded in 1849 as an army fort; grew as a cattle town on the Chisholm Trail — 'where the West begins'.
Its Stockyards hold twice-daily cattle drives.
Home to the Kimbell Art Museum and a major US money-printing facility.
Q211760: Capital of Sinaloa in northwest Mexico.
Founded in 1531, one of the oldest cities in northwest Mexico.
Centre of a rich farming region; also known as the base of the Sinaloa drug cartel.
Q5332: City on the Volga in southern Russia.
Historically a centre of the Volga Germans, who were deported in 1941.
Yuri Gagarin studied here and landed near the city after his 1961 space flight.
Known for its conservatory and long Volga bridge.
Q197519: Famous for its apples and as the 'hometown of Chinese apples' in Yunnan.
Badly hit by the 2014 Ludian earthquake.
Q71204: City in southeastern Hubei on the Yangtze.
An old mining centre: the Tonglüshan copper mine was worked 3,000 years ago.
The Hanyeping company here was China's first modern steel complex (1908).
Called the 'cradle of Chinese modern industry'.
Q191204: City in the east of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq; Kurds call it Slemani.
Founded in 1784 by the Baban prince Ibrahim Pasha and named after his father.
Considered the cultural capital of Iraqi Kurdistan, home of Kurdish poets and journalism.
Surrounded by mountains; has the Amna Suraka museum on the Anfal campaign.
Q1718: Capital of North Rhine-Westphalia on the Rhine.
Known for fashion, art (the Düsseldorf art academy) and the Königsallee shopping street.
Has one of Europe's largest Japanese communities.
Famous for Altbier and its long Rhine promenade; rival of Cologne.
Q34750: City in northwestern Liaoning bordering Inner Mongolia.
Once had Asia's largest open-pit coal mine (Haizhou).
Known for agate carving — called China's agate capital.
Q336350: Capital of Sokoto State in northwestern Nigeria.
Seat of the Sokoto Caliphate founded by Usman dan Fodio in 1804.
Its Sultan is the spiritual leader of Nigeria's Muslims.
Known for leather goods: 'Morocco leather' was often made here.
Q496576: City in western Yunnan near Myanmar; historically called Yongchang.
A stop on the ancient Southern Silk Road and the WWII Burma Road; the Battle of Tengchong took place nearby.
Famous for coffee from the Lujiang valley and for the volcanoes and hot springs of Tengchong.
Q1028116: County-level city in Jiangsu under Taizhou.
Famous for its rapeseed flower fields on small islands (duotian) in the water.
Hometown of Shi Nai'an, believed author of 'Water Margin', and the painter Zheng Banqiao.
Q1794: Germany's financial centre on the Main River.
Home of the European Central Bank, the Bundesbank and the Frankfurt Stock Exchange.
German emperors were elected and crowned here; Goethe was born here.
Has the largest airport in Germany and the world's biggest book fair.
Q648298: Capital of Ituri Province in northeastern DR Congo, near Lake Albert.
Centre of the Ituri conflict between Hema and Lendu groups.
Hosts a large UN peacekeeping base; gold mining is nearby.
Q1022: Capital of Baden-Württemberg, in a valley of the Neckar River.
Birthplace of the car: Daimler and Benz; Mercedes-Benz and Porsche have their headquarters and museums here.
Known for vineyards inside the city, the Cannstatter Wasen beer festival and Swabian food.
Q27136: The main city of Al-Ahsa, the world's largest oasis, in eastern Saudi Arabia.
Al-Ahsa has about 2.5 million date palms and is a World Heritage Site.
Known for its old souq, Ibrahim Palace and the Al-Qarah Mountain caves.
Q515846: City in southern Shaanxi on the Han River.
Lies between the Qinling and Daba mountains; its Yinghu Lake is a reservoir.
Q694939: Capital of Al-Qadisiyyah Governorate in southern-central Iraq.
Founded as a guesthouse of the Khaza'il tribe.
Centre of a rice and grain farming region on the Euphrates.
Q9824: City in Tamil Nadu on the Kaveri River.
Called the 'Turmeric City': one of the world's largest turmeric markets.
Also a big textile and handloom trade centre.
Hometown of the social reformer Periyar E. V. Ramasamy.
Q416922: The largest prefecture by area in Hunan, in the west.
A major railway junction connecting Hunan with Guizhou and Chongqing.
Home to Dong and Miao minorities; Hongjiang ancient town is a famous old trading town.
Q23482: France's second city and largest port, on the Mediterranean.
Founded by Greeks from Phocaea as Massalia around 600 BC — the oldest city in France.
Gave its name to the French national anthem, La Marseillaise.
Famous for bouillabaisse, Marseille soap and the basilica Notre-Dame de la Garde.
Q40435: City in western New York on Lake Erie, near Niagara Falls.
Boomed as the western end of the Erie Canal (1825); one of the first US cities with electric street lights.
Q2360633: Headquarters of Sitamarhi district in northern Bihar, near Nepal.
Named after Sita, wife of Rama, who according to Hindu tradition was born here.
The Janaki temple at Punaura is a pilgrimage site.
Q206484: Capital of Ogun State, on the Ogun River north of Lagos.
Founded around 1830 by Egba refugees at the Olumo Rock, a hiding place in wars.
Home town of many famous Nigerians, such as Wole Soyinka and Fela Kuti.
Q271619: Capital of Perak, Malaysia, in the Kinta Valley.
Boomed as the centre of the world's richest tin-mining area in the 19th century.
Known for colonial buildings, white coffee and limestone cave temples.
Called the 'City of Millionaires' for its tin-mining fortunes.
Q72907: Industrial city in eastern Shanxi at the foot of the Taihang Mountains.
A coal-mining centre known for anthracite.
Niangziguan pass of the Great Wall is nearby.
Q36600: Seat of the Dutch government and royal residence, on the North Sea coast; Amsterdam is the official capital.
Called the 'international city of peace and justice': the International Court of Justice and International Criminal Court are here.
Its Mauritshuis museum holds Vermeer's 'Girl with a Pearl Earring'.
The beach resort Scheveningen is part of the city.
Q244232: Capital of Tabuk Province in northwestern Saudi Arabia, near Jordan.
The Prophet Muhammad led an expedition here in 630.
A stop on the Hejaz Railway; near the planned NEOM mega-project.
A farming area known for roses and fruit.
Q955745: Municipality of El Alto, Bolivia's second-largest city, on the Altiplano above La Paz at about 4,100 m.
One of the highest big cities in the world; home to La Paz's international airport.
Mostly Aymara; known for its colourful 'cholet' buildings and a huge Thursday/Sunday market.
Q249007: City in central Gansu on the Hexi Corridor of the Silk Road.
The famous bronze 'Flying Horse of Gansu' (Han dynasty) was found here.
Called Liangzhou in history; a centre of early Buddhism in China (Kumarajiva lived here).
Q58324: An archipelago city off the coast of Zhejiang, at the mouth of Hangzhou Bay.
Mount Putuo, one of the Four Sacred Buddhist Mountains, is on an island here.
China's largest fishing ground and home of a big seafood industry.
Connected to the mainland by long sea bridges.
Q426237: City in northern Sichuan, the 'northern gate' of the province.
Hometown of Wu Zetian, China's only empress regnant; the Huangze Temple honours her.
The Jianmen Pass, a key fortress of the Three Kingdoms era, is in the prefecture.
Q200718: City in the Thar Desert of Rajasthan.
Founded in 1488 by Rao Bika; Junagarh Fort was never conquered.
Famous for bhujia snacks and camel breeding (National Research Centre on Camel).
The Karni Mata 'rat temple' is nearby in Deshnoke.
Q498004: District of Guangzhou in the northern suburbs, formerly Hua County.
Home of Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport.
Hometown of Hong Xiuquan, leader of the Taiping Rebellion.
Q40816: Libya's second city, on the Gulf of Sidra in Cyrenaica.
Founded by Greeks; refounded as Berenice under the Ptolemies.
Where the 2011 uprising against Gaddafi began.
Q79867: The largest metro area in Alabama.
Founded in 1871 and named after Birmingham, England; grew as a steel city ('Magic City').
A centre of the civil rights movement: the 1963 Birmingham campaign and the 16th Street Baptist Church bombing.
Its Vulcan statue is the largest cast-iron statue in the world.
Q7449155: Residential town in northern Singapore on the Straits of Johor.
Was home to a major British naval base from the 1930s.
Has Singapore's only natural hot spring (Sembawang Hot Spring Park).
Q404429: City in northern Henan, north of the Yellow River.
Home of Chenjiagou, birthplace of tai chi (Chen-style taijiquan).
Yuntai Mountain, a UNESCO Global Geopark with gorges and waterfalls, is nearby.
Former coal-mining town turned tourism city.
Q214248: City on Angola's Atlantic coast, capital of Benguela Province.
Founded by the Portuguese in 1617; a major slave-trade port.
Western end of the Benguela Railway to the Congo copper belt.
Next to the port city of Lobito.
Q856003: Royal city of Selangor, Malaysia, on the Klang River west of Kuala Lumpur.
The old capital of Selangor; still seat of the Sultan's palace.
Next to Port Klang, Malaysia's busiest port.
Famous for bak kut teh (pork rib soup).
Q49236: City on the Pinellas peninsula in the Tampa Bay area, Florida.
Holds a Guinness record for the most consecutive sunny days (768 days); called the 'Sunshine City'.
Home of the Salvador Dalí Museum.
The world's first scheduled commercial airline flight went from here to Tampa in 1914.
Q238508: Satellite city of Delhi in Haryana, officially Gurugram.
Grew from villages into a business hub since the 1980s, starting with the Maruti Suzuki car plant.
Has many multinational offices and malls (Cyber City).
The name links to Guru Dronacharya from the Mahabharata.
Q43199: The largest city in Nebraska, on the Missouri River.
Called the 'Gateway to the West'; the Union Pacific Railroad started its transcontinental line here.
Home of Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway and its yearly meeting.
Hosts the College World Series of baseball.
Q1028088: District of Shantou in eastern Guangdong.
China's 'toy capital': a large share of China's toys are made here.
Ancestral home of many overseas Teochew Chinese.
Q23443: City in Utah south of Salt Lake City, at the foot of the Wasatch Mountains.
Home of Brigham Young University and the Church's largest Missionary Training Center.
Part of the 'Silicon Slopes' tech area.
Q192961: Capital of Al Anbar Governorate in central Iraq, on the Euphrates.
Saw heavy fighting in the Iraq War and was largely destroyed when retaken from ISIS in 2015–16.
Q1774: Semi-autonomous archipelago of Tanzania off East Africa, called the 'Spice Islands'.
Was an independent sultanate and centre of the clove and slave trade; united with Tanganyika in 1964 to form Tanzania.
The Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896 is the shortest war in history (about 40 minutes).
Stone Town is a World Heritage Site.
Q695623: Capital of Barinas state, the 'capital of the Llanos' plains in Venezuela.
Birthplace region of Hugo Chávez, whose family dominated state politics.
Centre of cattle ranching and llanero music.
Q234600: The largest inland city of the UAE, in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi on the border with Oman.
Called the 'Garden City' for its oases and parks; the name means 'the spring'.
Its oasis and old sites (Hili, Jebel Hafeet tombs) are a World Heritage Site.
Birthplace of Sheikh Zayed, founder of the UAE.
Q42773: County-level city in Jiangsu between Suzhou and Shanghai.
China's richest county-level city for many years, with many Taiwanese electronics factories.
Birthplace of Kunqu, the oldest form of Chinese opera.
Zhouzhuang, a famous water town, is part of it.
Q219574: Municipality of the State of Mexico, just northwest of Mexico City.
The Tlatilco archaeological site has some of Mesoamerica's oldest figurines.
Home of the Torres de Satélite sculpture, symbol of Ciudad Satélite.
The name means 'place of the four neighbourhoods'.
Q2003745: City on the Kabul River in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, east of Peshawar.
A historic British army cantonment on the Grand Trunk Road.
Badly hit by the 2010 Pakistan floods.
Q168866: University city in northwestern Turkey on the Porsuk River; the name means 'old city'.
Known for meerschaum stone, used to carve pipes.
Odunpazarı, its Ottoman wooden-house quarter, is a tourist attraction.
Has a high-speed train to Ankara and Istanbul.
